answer: A sybil-resistant registry makes every agent lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a reef that only grows where coral commits to one rock: the deposit is trivial for one honest identity but multiplies for every mirror copy an attacker spins up, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand stakes. Peers attest to work, and if an agent cheats its stake is slashed and the reputation vine linking it to others withers, since no honest agent keeps vouching for a copy that burned them. Attack cost scales linearly while honest participation stays cheap.
